LESSON: VIRTUES GENEROSITY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Topic 5.1: Virtues Generosity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Virtues Generosity, part of Akhlaq (Moral Teachings) in Grade 5 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why should a Muslim practise generosity? 2. When should a Muslim practise generosity?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. assess the importance of practising generosity in the life of a Muslim,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues Generosity in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. practise generosity as a virtue for character formation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues Generosity in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the virtue of generosity as a means of earning rewards from Allah.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues Generosity in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. assess the importance of practising generosity in the life of a Muslim,

   Virtues Generosity helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. practise generosity as a virtue for character formation,

   Virtues Generosity helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the virtue of generosity as a means of earning rewards from Allah.

   Virtues Generosity helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. narrate short stories portraying generosity,

2. watch/listen to a story on generosity and deduce the teachings,

3. discuss the importance of observing generosity, and present in class,

4. participate in activities that involve practising generosity,

5. role-play activities that encourage generosity. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. narrate short stories portraying generosity,
2. watch/listen to a story on generosity and deduce the teachings,
3. discuss the importance of observing generosity, and present in class,
4. participate in activities that involve practising generosity,
5. role-play activities that encourage generosity. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Virtues Generosity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: enhanced as learners participate in activities that involve practising generosity.

• Self-efficacy: skill of sharing learnt knowledge is enhanced as learners narrate short stories portraying generosity.

• Creativity and innovation: the skill of networking is enhanced as learners role-play activities that encourage generosity.

Values:
Rresponsibility as learners participate in activities that involve practising generosity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: as learners participate in activities that involve practising generosity

Links to other Learning Areas:
Creative Arts as learners role-play activities that encourage generosity.
